title: Telegram API pricing in 2026: what is free and what you pay for
snippet:
| What | Price |
|---|---|
| Bot API, Telegram API (MTProto) | Free, no request or user limits on billing |
| Messages within the free limits | Free, about 30 messages per second |
| Paid broadcasts above 30 per second | 0.1 Stars per delivered message |
| Login codes through Telegram Gateway | $0.01 per delivered code |
| Payments for physical goods | No Telegram fee, only the payment provider’s commission |
| Digital goods for Stars | No Telegram fee, developers withdraw $0.013 per Star |
| Bot API server for large files | Free code, you pay for your own hosting |
| Bot replies for a Business account | The account needs Telegram Premium |

| API | What it is for | How to get access | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bot API | Bots and Mini Apps: messages, buttons, payments, groups, channels | A token from @BotFather | Free |
| Telegram API (MTProto) | Your own Telegram client or work on behalf of a user account | api_id and api_hash at my.telegram.org | Free |
| TDLib | A ready library for building clients on top of MTProto | Open source, built into your app | Free |

The free tier has limits on speed and file size.
- **About 30 messages per second** to different users and **about one message per second** to a single chat. In groups a bot sends up to 20 messages per minute.
- **A broadcast to 10,000 subscribers** takes around six minutes at these limits. For most businesses this is enough.
- **Files:** a bot downloads files up to 20 MB and uploads up to 50 MB through the standard Bot API.
The file limit is removed with your own Bot API server. Telegram publishes its code for free, and with it a bot uploads files up to 2 GB. You pay only for the hosting.

Digital goods and services inside Telegram are sold for Stars under the platform rules: subscriptions, access to content, paid bot features. Telegram itself takes no commission, but users buy Stars through Apple and Google with their store fees included. Developers withdraw Stars through Fragment at $0.013 per Star, paid in Toncoin. A Star can be withdrawn 21 days after it was received, and the minimum withdrawal is 1,000 Stars. A user who buys 1,000 Stars in the App Store pays about $20, and the developer receives about $13 for them. Plan prices with this gap in mind.

Since the API is free, the main expense is development: scenarios, payments, integrations with your CRM and inventory, an admin panel.

title: Telegram API Terms of Service
snippet:
We welcome all developers to use our API and source code to [create Telegram-like messaging applications](https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id) on our platform free of charge. In order to ensure consistency and security across the Telegram ecosystem, all third-party client apps must comply with the following Terms of Service.

**2.1.** You must [obtain your own api_id](https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id#obtaining-api-id) for your application.
**2.2.** We offer our API free of charge, but your users must be aware of the fact that your app uses the Telegram API and is part of the Telegram ecosystem. This fact must be featured prominently in the app's description in the app stores and in the in-app intro if your app has it.

title: Telegram APIs
snippet:
We offer three kinds of APIs for developers. The **Bot API** allows you to easily create programs that use Telegram messages for an interface. The **Telegram API and TDLib** allow you to build your own customized Telegram clients. You are welcome to use both APIs free of charge. Lastly, the **Gateway API** allows any business, app or website to send verification codes through Telegram instead of traditional SMS.

This API allows you to connect bots to our system. [**Telegram Bots**](https://policies.telegram.org/bots) are special accounts that do not require an additional phone number to set up. These accounts serve as an interface for code running somewhere on your server.
To use this, you don't need to know anything about how our MTProto encryption protocol works — our intermediary server will handle all encryption and communication with the Telegram API for you. You communicate with this server via a simple HTTPS interface that offers a simplified version of the Telegram API.
Bot developers can also make use of our [**Payments API**](https://policies.telegram.org/bots/payments) to accept **payments** from Telegram users around the world.

This API allows you to build your own customized Telegram clients. It is 100% open for all developers who wish to create Telegram applications on our platform. Feel free to study the open [source code](https://telegram.org/apps#source-code) of existing Telegram applications for examples of how things work here. Don't forget to [register](https://policies.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id) your application in our system.

#### [Telegram Premium](https://policies.telegram.org/api/premium)
Telegram Premium is an optional subscription service that unlocks additional exclusive client-side and API-side features, while helping support the development of the app. It is a part of Telegram’s **sustainable monetization** – driven by our users, rather than advertisers or shareholders. This way, Telegram can remain independent and prioritize its users first.

title: Creating your Telegram Application
snippet:
We welcome all developers to use our [API](https://core.telegram.org/api#telegram-api) and source code to create Telegram-like messaging applications on our platform free of charge.
> In order to ensure consistency and security across the Telegram ecosystem, **all third-party client apps** must comply with the [**API Terms of Service**](/api/terms).
### Obtaining api_id
In order to obtain an **API id** and develop your own application using the Telegram API you need to do the following:
- Sign up for Telegram using an official application.
- Log in to your Telegram core: [https://my.telegram.org](https://my.telegram.org).
- Go to ["API development tools"](https://my.telegram.org/apps) and fill out the form.
- You will get basic addresses as well as the **api_id** and **api_hash** parameters required for user authorization.
- For the moment each number can only have one api_id connected to it.
We will be sending important developer notifications to the phone number that you use in this process, so please use an up-to-date number connected to your active Telegram account.
